title: Shallow Clones
description: Use shallow clones to clone only the latest commits and drastically reduce clone time and disk usage.

data.text: git clone --depth <N> creates a shallow clone that includes only the last N commits from the specified branch. This reduces clone time from minutes to seconds and disk usage from gigabytes to megabytes, at the cost of not having the full history.
The --depth flag controls how many commits to include. --depth 1 clones only the latest commit (the branch tip). Larger values include more history.

data.title: Clone with different depths
data.code:
# Shallow clone: only the latest commit
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/example/project.git

# Shallow clone: last 10 commits
git clone --depth 10 https://github.com/example/project.git

# Shallow clone a specific branch
git clone --depth 1 --branch feature/auth https://github.com/example/project.git

# Clone with a specific tag
git clone --depth 1 --branch v2.1.0 https://github.com/example/project.git

data.text: Converting a shallow clone to a full clone
If you initialized with a shallow clone but later need the full history, use git fetch --unshallow to download the remaining commits.

data.title: Unshallow a repository
data.code:
# Fetch the full history
git fetch --unshallow

# Or fetch to a specific depth
git fetch --depth=100

# Verify the repository is now full
git rev-list --count HEAD

# Check that objects are complete
git fsck --full

items: **No push**: Shallow clones cannot push because the history is incomplete
**No full merge**: Some merge operations require the full history
**Limited bisect**: git bisect cannot start without a good commit in the history
**No reflog**: Shallow clones have a limited or no reflog

data.title: Attempting to push from a shallow clone fails
data.code:
# Shallow clone
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/example/project.git
cd project

# Make a change
git add .
git commit -m "fix: update config"

# Try to push — this FAILS
git push origin main

# Error:
# ! [remote rejected] main -> main (shallow update not allowed)

# Solution: unshallow before pushing
git fetch --unshallow
git push origin main

data.text: CI systems that build pull requests or run tests only need the latest commit. Use shallow clones to reduce checkout time and save bandwidth.

data.title: GitHub Actions with shallow clone
data.code:
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 1

# For pull_request events, this fetches only the PR head
# For push events, this fetches only the latest commit

# Total checkout time drops from 30s to 5s
# for repositories with large histories

data.text: git clone --filter=<spec> creates a partial clone that downloads the full history but omits certain file contents. This gives you the ability to bisect and log while saving disk space. See the partial-clone lesson for details.

items.question: Can I fetch new commits in a shallow clone?
items.answer: Yes. Use git pull to fetch new commits from the remote, but the clone remains shallow. Use git fetch --depth=<N> to deepen the history.

items.question: Does --depth work with --branch?
items.answer: Yes. Use both flags together to clone a specific branch at a specific depth.

items.question: Can I push tags from a shallow clone?
items.answer: Tags can be pushed, but the tag must reference a commit that exists in the shallow clone. Annotated tags require the tagged object to be present.

items.question: What is the difference between shallow and partial clone?
items.answer: Shallow clone truncates history (fewer commits). Partial clone downloads full history but omits file contents. Use shallow clone for CI; use partial clone when you need history but not all files.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: git clone --depth <N> creates a shallow clone with the last N commits
git fetch --unshallow converts a shallow clone to a full clone
Shallow clones cannot push until they are unshallowed
Use shallow clones in CI to reduce checkout time
Partial clones (--filter) are the middle ground: full history, selective files
